## This week online, we are learning how to download maps from satellite services

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

## Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(sf)
library(maptiles)
library(tidyterra)
library(leaflet)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(ggspatial)
library(praise)
```
```{r}
## Load and view data
ChemData <- read_csv(here("Week_07", "Data", "chemicaldata_maunalua.csv"))

glimpse(ChemData)
```

## Step 1 - Define the area of interest
```{r}
## Define your bounding box for the spatial data
wailupe_bbox <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(
  xmin = -157.772, ymin = 21.267,
  xmax = -157.752, ymax = 21.281),
  crs = 4326))
```

## Step 2 - Download the tiles
```{r}
## Download the tiles for your map
tiles_satellite <- get_tiles(wailupe_bbox,
  provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
  zoom = 16,
  crop = TRUE,
  cachedir = here("Week_07","Data","tiles_cache"))
```

## Step 3 - Plot the tiles
```{r}
## Plot the tiles using ggplot and geom_spatraster_rgb
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = tiles_satellite) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Practice deriving the bounding box from the data itself
```{r}
## Convert your data frame to an sf object
ChemData_sf <- st_as_sf(ChemData,
                         coords = c("Long", "Lat"),
                         crs = 4326)
```
```{r}
## Get your bounding box and add a small buffer so points are not at the edges of the map
bbox_chem <- st_bbox(ChemData_sf) + c(-0.004, -0.004, 0.004, 0.004)
```
```{r}
## Download the tiles for your specified bounding box
Map_satellite <- get_tiles(
  st_as_sfc(bbox_chem),
  provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
  zoom = 15,
  crop = TRUE,
  cachedir = here("Week_07", "data", "tiles_cache")
)
```

## Overlay point data onto a tile basemap
```{r}
## Polish your point data on your map
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster_rgb(data = Map_satellite) +
  geom_point(data = ChemData,
             aes(x = Long, y = Lat,
                 color = Salinity),
             size = 4) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name = "Salinity (ppt)") +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl",        
    bar_cols = c("yellow", "white")) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl") +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326) +
  labs(title = "Maunalua Bay — Water Chemistry",
       caption = "Basemap: ESRI World Imagery") +
  theme_minimal()

## Save your map
ggsave(here("Week_07", "Outputs", "maunalua_map.pdf"), width = 8, height = 6)
```

## Create an interactive leaflet map
```{r}
## Create a leaflet centered with setView on Wailupe
leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  setView(lng = -157.762, lat = 21.274, zoom = 14)

## Add a color palette to convert numeric values to hex colors
pal <- colorNumeric(
  palette = "viridis",            # any RColorBrewer or viridis palette name
  domain = ChemData$Salinity      # the full range of values to map
)

## Use it by calling pal to see what hex colors a certain salinity would get
pal(30)

## Add data points with color
leaflet(ChemData) |>           # pass data frame here
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~Long, lat = ~Lat,   # which columns are coordinates
    color = ~pal(Salinity),    # apply our color function to Salinity
    radius = 6,
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~paste("Salinity:", Salinity, "ppt",  # click a point to see this
                   "<br>Site:", Site)) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = pal,                 # the same color function
    values = ~Salinity,        # which column drives the legend
    title = "Salinity (ppt)",
    position = "bottomright")
```

## Practice geocoding
```{r}
## Practice calling UH Mānoa for geocoding
geo("University of Hawaii at Manoa", method = "osm")

## Create a tribble of places
oahu_sites <- tribble(
  ~place,
  "University of Hawaii at Manoa",
  "Honolulu International Airport",
  "Pearl Harbor National Memorial, Hawaii",
  "Diamond Head State Monument, Hawaii"
)

## Call Oʻahu sites you created with the tribble
oahu_geocoded <- oahu_sites |>
  geocode(place, method = "osm")   # geocode the 'place' column

## Look at your tbl to see the coordinates of each place you called
oahu_geocoded
```

## Map your geocoded locations
```{r}
leaflet(oahu_geocoded) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~long, lat = ~lat,   # tidygeocoder always returns 'lat' and 'long'
    label = ~place)            # hover to see place name
```

## That's all for today! Yay mapping!
